title: The Witness of Creation
english: How could God tolerate the wicked deeds of Israel?

God will testify against them, calling heaven and earth as witnesses, because He is about to rebuke Israel and make known to the angels in heaven and to the whole earth the ways of Israel's wickedness, so that no one would think that the beloved people, who had been chosen as His inheritance and who possessed noble birth, were being rejected for no reason or for minor and insignificant transgressions.
For God had pity on Israel as one who was being wronged, and He had freed them from the Egyptians' oppression through great power.

But when the Egyptians retaliated, they were severely punished by God, who armed creation against those who hated Him with many signs, both many and marvelous, in heaven and on earth, including hail from heaven and frogs from the earth, as it is written (Exodus 7:19-8:2).
The water was also being turned into blood, and a furnace of burning coal was being kindled, and the air was being darkened, with sores and blisters rising up on the bodies of all people.
Just as the reception of Israel was notable, so God wants the manner of their rejection to be known.

If some people want to call the elements themselves to witness through the prophet's voice, the power of the proper meaning of the notions would not have been missed, though it had been obscured, for the elements had toiled in vain over those who had been redeemed.
For Israel was redeemed from the Egyptians' wickedness through Moses.
But when Pharaoh resisted God's signs and said, 'I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go,' creation was armed against those who hated God.

The Israelites, having despised the training of the law and having neglected the teachings of salvation, and having left the one true God, were offering worship to unclean demons in mountains and hills, and in the most wooded valleys, sacrificing and prostrating themselves to the works of their own hands.
And the God of all was grieving over these things, and very rightly so.
He said to one of the holy prophets, 'Arise and plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice' (Micah 6:1).
'Hear, O mountains, the judgment of the Lord, and you, O valleys, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a case against His people' (Micah 6:2).
'Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken' (Isaiah 1:2).

title: The Shepherds' Folly and the Reproach of Jerusalem
english: …It became for me an unapproachable wilderness. It resulted in destruction and loss. For the shepherds were truly foolish and did not seek the Lord; because of this, the whole flock did not understand and was scattered. The shepherds were indeed foolish, and they became a cause of destruction for the people under their hand.

Moreover, how was it that they should not have been a way for others to believe in Christ, having been greatly instructed through law and prophets, to be a path for others to believe in him? Or does the Savior say that he received glory from man and did not seek the glory that comes from God alone? For if they believed in Moses, they would have believed in him, for he wrote about him. They have indeed become blind and leaders of the blind. In this way they have also slipped and have fallen into the pits of destruction.

What then does the prophet attempt to do by advising them with good exhortations: to cause the declining to think well, and to test the words of the Savior? He mixes, however, the rebuke with the exhortations in a medicinal way, with a varied remedy, healing the wounds of their evil counsel. Thus, he says, 'Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; attend to the law of God, people of Gomorrah.' You hear how he brings a rod of love and divine thought to the people and rulers, and strikes many who are diseased with disobedience.

To the most impious cities, he exhorts Jerusalem, as being the greatest in immeasurable sin and not having anyone completely righteous within itself… For God was planning to destroy the cities of the Sodomites and made the matter known to Abraham; and he [responded] to Him, 'Will you destroy the righteous with the wicked? And shall the righteous be as the wicked?' (Genesis 18:24-25). God promised that if ten righteous people were found in Sodom, He would spare the cities from His wrath. But He did not find them. For they had received punishments equal to their own impieties. Such was the condition of Jerusalem, having a small portion of the righteous.

And indeed the prophet Jeremiah lamented for her. And God said, 'Run through the streets of Jerusalem, and see, and seek, and look in her squares, if you find a man who does justice and seeks faith, so that I may be merciful to her' (Jeremiah 5:1). Because, therefore, she is defiled and has been polluted in many ways by impurities of filthiness, and having a large portion of the saints, He calls her both Sodom and Gomorrah, both to the people and to the leaders, bringing the reproach of the uncleanness of the Sodomites upon them. And what does he indeed say? 'Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; attend to the law of God, people of Go…
translator_notes: The text begins and ends mid-sentence; ellipses indicate missing fragments.
The phrase 'ήν μου εἰς ἔρημον ἄβατον' is rendered as 'It became for me an unapproachable wilderness'.
The clause 'ἐγενήθη εἰς ἀφανισμὸν ἀπωλείας' denotes the result of the shepherds' foolishness.
The dialogue between Abraham and God is a direct quotation of Genesis 18:24-25.
The quotation from Jeremiah is a direct quotation of Jeremiah 5:1.
The phrase 'ἐβουλεύετο μὲν γὰρ ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς' refers to God's counsel or plan regarding the destruction of the cities.

title: Apostasy of Zion
english: …disobedient and hard of hearing; how did faithful Zion, full of judgment, become a prostitute city; formerly righteousness was asleep in it, now it is murderous. It marvels at the Jews' transition, which is a wretched and not a regular change, a movement from the better to the worse, and a transition from the unashamed to the shameful. For through Moses, the law once provided a knowledge of what is beneficial, and having a minister of the word of God for every practical matter, it was shining, most prosperous, and worthy, being distinguished among most men, to whom the fruit of righteousness was richly produced, and it was acceptable to God. For there were in it both prophets and priests, and those who meditated on the works of righteousness, and leaders of the people guarding judgment, having the law upon the tongue, and being instructed in every way both kind and good.

Now, being deprived of such things, it has instead fallen into the folly of abandoning that ancient moderation, and has been laid low by nothing less than the abandonment of its fear toward God and its love; and before the arrival of our Savior, it prostrated itself to those who are not gods by nature, utterly violating the one and true Lord through fornications directed toward this. Like a woman who is much-frequented and has been revered, she has acted impiously in many ways. At various times, she has been attached to different teachers, possessing the knowledge of conveying whatever has been preached by God. Indeed, she is accused through the voice of Jeremiah, the God of all things, saying: 'Behold what the house of Israel has done to me; it has gone upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and has committed fornication there' (Jeremiah 3:6).

And again to her: 'If a man sends away his wife, and she, having gone from him, becomes a man's other, will she not still be called to him? Will that woman not be defiled? You have committed fornication with many shepherds, and you have not uncovered yourself before me, says the Lord. Lift up your eyes to the straight way, and see where you have not been ravished; you sat upon the roads to them, like a solitary crow in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your fornications and your evils, and you have had many shepherds as a stumbling block to yourself. The appearance of a prostitute has become yours; you have become shameless before all' (Jeremiah 3:12-24).

For, as I have said, despising the servitude under God, it turned toward apostasy and toward unclean spirits and toward the healers of idols, using shepherds and teachers. And these, as I have said, were the crimes of the Jewish Synagogue before the arrival of our Savior. But since Christ has shone upon those on the earth (for God the Lord has appeared to us, according to what is written), it did not use him more as a teacher; rather, it valued teachings and commandments…
